headline: What is a pulse doing?
subhead: THE QUESTION UNDER ALL OF THIS
body: So by now we know pulses grow more bone than a flat level at the same total dose, in multiple species and multiple labs. What nobody in that older literature could answer is what a pulse is physically doing that a flat level is not. | A 2023 paper answered it at the level of the DNA itself, and the answer is considerably more literal than anything I expected when I went looking for it.
punch: What is a pulse doing that a flat level is not?

headline: Your DNA is not always readable
body: Your DNA is wound tightly around proteins rather than sitting loose. For a gene to be read at all, that stretch of DNA has to physically open up and become accessible. If it stays wound shut then it does not matter what signal arrives at the cell, because nothing can reach the gene. | *Chromatin accessibility* is the measurement of which stretches are open at any given moment. And GH pulses turn out to control it directly.
punch: A gene that is closed cannot be read.

headline: The experiment
subhead: REMOVE THE PITUITARY, THEN ONE DOSE
body: Take the pituitary out of a mouse and the GH pulses stop completely. When that happens, thousands of regions of DNA in the liver physically close up, which the researchers could measure directly. | Then they gave **a single physiological replacement dose of GH**. Not a course of treatment, not a week of dosing. One pulse, at a normal physiological size, and then they looked at what happened to the DNA.

headline: What did one pulse do?
body: That single dose restored STAT5 activity and chromatin accessibility at **83%** of the dynamic male-biased regions that had closed after the pituitary was removed. More than **3,500 sites** opened within half an hour of one injection. | What this means is that the response is not a slow adaptation over days of treatment. One pulse, thirty minutes, thousands of genes become readable that were not readable before it arrived.
punch: ==One pulse reopened 83% of them in 30 minutes.==

headline: Then it closes again
body: This is the part that explains the entire pulsatility literature. The regions open when the pulse arrives and then close again in the gap before the next one. The paper calls it a **dynamic cycle of opening and closing**. | A flat GH level cannot produce a cycle, by definition. It produces one state, held constant. So the thing a pulse delivers that an infusion cannot is not a higher concentration. It is a transition.
punch: The cycle is the signal. Not the level.

headline: The trough is not downtime
body: If the opening is driven by the arrival of a pulse, then you need the closing in order to get another arrival. A constant level is not a very long pulse. It is the absence of pulses. | The authors state it directly: **the pulsatility of plasma GH stimulation per se** confers the pattern of accessibility. Which also explains Bick's receptor data from the other post, where occupied receptors were highest right after a pulse and lower 90 minutes later.
punch: _The gap is what makes the next pulse readable._

headline: Be precise about this
body: This was measured in mouse **liver**, and the specific subject is sex-biased liver gene expression rather than anything to do with the growth plate. That is a real limitation and it should be stated plainly rather than buried. | What the paper establishes is the mechanism by which a pulse differs from a flat level at all, in any tissue. Extending that to cartilage is an inference, and it is labelled as one here rather than presented as a finding.
punch: Liver. Mouse. A mechanism, not a protocol.

headline: What this explains
body: A GH pulse is not simply a higher number held for a shorter time. It is a physical event that opens DNA and then allows it to close again, and the closing is as necessary as the opening. | That is the cleanest answer anyone has for why the same total dose, delivered flat, consistently does less. Not because the concentration is wrong, but because a flat delivery has no transitions in it.
punch: ==A pulse is an event. A level is just a number.==
